sections.text: println! prints text followed by a new line. Curly braces {} inside the text are placeholders that get filled in with values.
Both lines print the same thing. You can list values after the text, or put a variable's name straight inside the braces.
A variable is a name for a value, as you saw in Unit 0. Here name holds the text "Ferris" and age holds the number 8. The next lesson takes a closer look at changing variables.

Coming from another language: {name} works like f-strings in Python or template literals in JavaScript, but the format string is checked at compile time. A typo in a placeholder is a compile error, not a runtime surprise. Only a plain variable name fits inside the braces (unlike f-strings and template literals, which take any expression): {age + 1} is an error. For anything else, use {} and pass the value after the string: println!("{}", age + 1).
print! is the same but without the new line. eprintln! prints to the error stream. {:?} prints a value in a debug form, which is handy for a group of values like this one (an array; more in Unit 2):

Coming from another language: the app shows rustc warnings apart from your program's output, and they never stop the program. In exercises, an unused-variable warning usually just means you haven't finished yet. Ignore the advice to prefix the name with an underscore: that hides the warning instead of fixing your code.

exercise.prompt: Use the variables to print exactly: Ferris has 3 friends
hints: Right now the text between the quotes of println! is empty, so only an empty line prints.
Put a variable's name inside {} in the text. Inside the quotes, write {name} where the name goes.
Fill the quotes with {name} has {friends} friends. Make sure the spaces match the expected output.

quiz.question: What does {} do inside println!?
options: Starts a new block of code
Marks where a value is inserted
quiz.explanation: {} is a placeholder: println! puts the matching value there. To print literal curly braces you have to write them doubled, as {{ and }}.

quiz.question: What does println!("{:?}", [1, 2]) print?
quiz.explanation: {:?} uses the Debug format, which prints the array as [1, 2], brackets and commas included. The plain {} would not compile for an array because it has no ordinary display format.

quiz.question: How is print! different from println!?
options: It doesn't add a new line
quiz.explanation: print! writes its text without a new line at the end, so the next output continues on the same line. println! adds the new line. They print the same kinds of values.
